I will do it mostly the way that has worked here, then adjust a little for cost and water. On my 10.1 mu, I will keep most of the land in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because that is the steady income and I know how to manage it. I will leave a smaller piece for cotton, because cotton takes more watching and more spraying, and with only 2 people at home I cannot spread myself too thin. I have middle school education, so I do look at seed, fertilizer, and yield a bit more carefully than just copying old habit, but I still start from what I used before and what nearby farmers got good results with. Since I have well irrigation, I will not be too stingy with water on wheat jointing and filling, and I will not cut fertilizer too hard, because losing yield hurts more than wasting a little fertilizer. For wheat I will use improved seed, fairly solid nitrogen, enough phosphorus for roots, and a little potassium. For summer maize I will use hybrid seed, because the hybrids around here usually stand better and fill better if water keeps up. I will sow maize right after wheat and keep field work simple, mostly no-tillage or very light work, to save time. For cotton I will keep the area smaller, use improved seed, feed it more evenly, and spray more times because insects can ruin it fast if I wait.
